title: An AI eye exam increased screening among young people with diabetes
summary: In the ACCESS trial, all 81 young people offered IDx-DR completed an eye exam, compared with 18 of 82 controls referred to an eye-care provider.
account: The ACCESS trial enrolled young people with diabetes at two Johns Hopkins clinics in Baltimore. Of 164 participants randomized, one control was excluded after entering another screening study. All 81 participants assigned to an IDx-DR eye exam completed screening, compared with 18 of 82 controls referred to an eye-care provider. The AI marked 25 results as positive, and 16 of those participants attended an eye-care visit within six months. A retina specialist reviewed all AI images for safety because the device was not cleared for this age group. The study measured screening and follow-up, not preserved vision.
purpose: IDx-DR/LumineticsCore is built to autonomously detect more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy from fundus images at the point of care. Increasing screening completion is its intended benefit.
segment: Autonomous AI screening in pediatric diabetes care
taxonomy_note: The trial reports exam completion and follow-through, process outcomes, rather than vision outcomes.

ratings.reason: The trial measured a substantial increase in completed diabetic eye exams. It did not establish improved vision or prevention of blindness.

ai_role.statement: IDx-DR assessed retinal photographs and returned a screening result during the diabetes visit. The trial compared this on-site service with referral elsewhere. A retina specialist also reviewed the images for safety. A coauthor had financial interests in the manufacturer, although he did not have access to the underlying data.
